configfiles.configfile:
# LibreQDA configuration for the Galaxy interactive tool. `libreqda server` # execs this file before the application is built, so it can also adjust # application classes (see the Galaxy adaptation at the end).
import os import secrets
import taguette.web.base import tornado.web
# --- LibreQDA settings ---
NAME = 'LibreQDA' PORT = 7465 BIND_ADDRESS = '0.0.0.0' SECRET_KEY = secrets.token_hex(32)
# Everything LibreQDA stores lives in this single SQLite database: projects, # documents, highlights, tags and codebooks. It is written straight into the # Galaxy output dataset ($database_out), which is copied to the history when the # session ends, so nothing has to be collected from the working directory. _OUTPUT_DB = os.path.abspath('$database_out') DATABASE = 'sqlite:///' + _OUTPUT_DB
# No terms-of-service page, no outgoing mail and no cookie banner: there is a # single pre-authenticated user (see UNIX_SOCKET below). TOS_FILE = None X_HEADERS = False EMAIL = 'LibreQDA <noreply@localhost>' MAIL_SERVER = dict(ssl=False, host='localhost', port=25) COOKIES_PROMPT = False MULTIUSER = False
# Upstream reads this flag as "I run behind an authenticating reverse proxy": # it skips the application access token, which is otherwise printed once to # stdout and has to be appended to the URL as ?token=... Galaxy's interactive # tool URL is already unguessable and authenticated, so the token only adds # friction. This does NOT move the listener to a unix socket; the application # keeps listening on TCP (see BIND_ADDRESS and PORT above). UNIX_SOCKET = True
# --- Galaxy adaptation --- # # Galaxy embeds the entry point in an iframe on a different origin. Three # upstream defaults defeat that embed. They are only changed when UNIX_SOCKET # is set, so upstream behaviour is untouched otherwise.
if UNIX_SOCKET: # 1. Cookies are emitted without a SameSite attribute, which browsers # treat as Lax. Lax cookies are never sent on a cross-origin iframe # navigation, so the "no session yet, log in and redirect to /" branch # loops forever (ERR_TOO_MANY_REDIRECTS). def _galaxy_cookies(original): def set_cookie(handler, name, value, *args, **kwargs): kwargs.setdefault('samesite', 'None') kwargs.setdefault('secure', True) return original(handler, name, value, *args, **kwargs)
return set_cookie
tornado.web.RequestHandler.set_cookie = _galaxy_cookies( tornado.web.RequestHandler.set_cookie)
# 2. In UNIX_SOCKET mode every request is pre-authenticated by the trusted # proxy, so the current user is always "admin" instead of coming from a # session cookie round trip. This also keeps the application usable when # the browser blocks third-party cookies. taguette.web.base.BaseHandler.get_current_user = lambda self: 'admin'
# 3. Headers send X-Frame-Options: DENY and CSP frame-ancestors 'none' # (clickjacking protection), which makes browsers refuse to render the # application inside the Galaxy iframe. The unguessable interactive tool # host remains the access boundary. def _galaxy_frame_headers(original): def set_default_headers(handler): original(handler) handler.clear_header('X-Frame-Options') handler.set_header('Content-Security-Policy', 'frame-ancestors *')
return set_default_headers
taguette.web.base.BaseHandler.set_default_headers = _galaxy_frame_headers( taguette.web.base.BaseHandler.set_default_headers)

tool.help:
`LibreQDA <https://gitlab.com/bin-cirst/libreqda/libre-qda>`_ is a free and open-source qualitative data analysis (QDA) tool developed by the Plateforme en humanités numériques (PHuN) at Université de Sherbrooke. It is a fork of `Taguette <https://taguette.org/>`_ with additions developed together with qualitative-analysis researchers: document collections, code hierarchies, overlaid coding stripes, drag-and-drop coding, an integrated search engine and faster multi-file import.
.. class:: infomark
**How to use it**
- Leave *LibreQDA database with previous work* empty to start a new project, or pick a database from an earlier session to continue where you left off. - Import your documents (PDF, DOCX, ODT, TXT, HTML, EPUB, MOBI, RTF), create tags and code the text inside the application, in your browser. - Exports (tagged excerpts, coded documents, ...) are downloaded through your browser as usual.
**Saving your work**
Everything you do is stored in one SQLite database (projects, documents, highlights, tags and codebooks). When the session ends, that database is written to your history as *LibreQDA database with all projects, documents and codes*. To continue the work later, start the tool again and select that dataset as *LibreQDA database with previous work* - nothing else has to be exported or re-imported.
.. class:: warning
The database is only copied to your history when the session ends. Documents that you import into the session are part of that database, so they are kept as well.
